transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-25
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jesse Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CobaltBank Head of Security), Leah Patel (CobaltBank Platform Eng), Samir Rao (Cobalt PM)

Summary:
Weekly POC security sync focused on SSO/SAML onboarding, audit log access for the pilot, data retention settings for the POC, and SOC2 evidence needed to support procurement. Redwood agreed to share audit log samples and SSO quickstart; CobaltBank to provision test IdP and confirm SOC2 stakeholders.

Topics:
- SSO / SAML setup progress and blockers
- Audit logs: schema, access, retention
- Data retention and deletion during POC
- SOC2 artifacts and evidence request process
- Next steps and owners

Action items (as discussed in call):
- Priya: produce audit log sample (CSV + schema)
- Jesse: SSO quickstart + SAML metadata, share security pack (SOC2 summary)
- Leah: create test IdP account and invite Redwood team
- Michael: identify internal audit stakeholders for SOC2 walkthrough

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick roll call — Priya you there?
[00:04] Priya: Yup, here.
[00:06] Michael: Michael on my end.
[00:08] Leah: Leah here.
[00:09] Samir: Samir, hey.
[00:12] Jesse: Cool. High level agenda: SSO status, audit logs access for the pilot (we heard Leah had questions), retention/deletion for POC, and then SOC2 artifact walk. Priya will cover the audit-log format and what Redwood exposes.
[00:25] Priya: Great. So on the audit logs — what Redwood exposes for the hosted POC is a streaming audit feed and daily export. The schema has event_time, request_id, user_id, route, model_variant, bytes_in, bytes_out, decision_flags, and a few other fields. We can export a CSV with redacted token fields for you to ingest into your SIEM.
[00:44] Leah: Quick question — are request and response bodies included? For compliance we need to know whether full prompt text is present in logs or just metadata.
[00:51] Priya: Good Q. By default we log metadata only; full user input can be optionally recorded in the audit stream but it's off for the POC unless you request it. Also we do prefix/redaction options — so we can redact PII or mask tokens.
[01:10] Michael: Ok that helps. For audit and legal we usually want metadata only for the POC. We'll want to see the schema and sample rows to confirm fields map to our SIEM.
[01:20] Priya: We'll provide a sample CSV with synthetic but realistic rows. Note there might be minor tokenization artifacts in timestamps — the exporter occasionally stamps in ms and sometimes the field name comes out as "evt_time" in older versions, sorry there's some historical mismatch, we'll normalize for you.
[01:35] Samir: That historical mismatch is fine as long as you call out the field mapping in the sample.
[01:40] Jesse: Great. Next SSO — last week Leah started the IdP provisioning and had an issue with the metadata upload. Leah, where are we?
[01:49] Leah: So I uploaded the metadata XML but Redwood's assertion consumer service URL didn't match the template in our IdP. I think that was just a URL encoding problem; I can repro and send you the exact error.
[02:02] Jesse: Ok we can take that offline but Priya can also share a quick checklist. We have a SSO quickstart that includes expected ACS URL, Entity ID, and sample SAML request/response.
[02:12] Priya: I'll drop that. Also note we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; for POC most customers use IdP-initiated while evaluating.
[02:22] Michael: For our internal audit we need SAML assertions to include email and employee_id. Is that doable?
[02:28] Priya: Yes, we can map attributes. There is a small mapping table we'll send. There is also a signed assertion requirement — we support signed assertions and encrypted NameID.
[02:40] Leah: One other ask — we need RBAC controls around team access, can we scope access to specific routes/models?
[02:46] Jesse: Yes, Redwood supports role-based policies and per-route permissions in the console and via the API. Priya, maybe mention the permission model briefly?
[02:53] Priya: Sure — Roles are at org or project level, and we can create fine-grained policies limiting who can call generate endpoints vs. who can view logs or manage billing. For the POC you'll likely map your teams to two roles: devs (generate) and auditors (read-only logs).
[03:12] Samir: That covers internal least privilege. On data retention — for POC, what options do we have to automatically purge request metadata after X days?
[03:20] Priya: We have a retention config per project. For hosted POC we can set retention to 7, 30, or 90 days; we can also set manual delete. For Private deployments you can set shorter retention via config. Note: token caches used for streaming are ephemeral and not stored in long-term logs.
[03:37] Michael: We prefer 30 days for the pilot. Also need to confirm deletion is irreversible and whether backups are retained longer.
[03:45] Priya: Deletion for logs is irreversible in the tenant view. Backups for disaster recovery have a separate lifecycle; for hosted POC we can request that long-term backups not retain PII and we can produce an attestation. We'll include language in the security pack.
[04:02] Leah: On the backups — is encryption at rest using our KMS supported during POC or only in Private?
[04:09] Jesse: For the hosted POC we use Redwood-managed encryption keys by default; however, we can enable customer-managed keys (KMIP/KMS) for Dedicated and Private. For some POC customers we have a short-term KMS integration for evaluation; we can surface that in the SOC2 pack but it's generally not enabled by default.
[04:29] Michael: We'll mark that as a blocker only if procurement requires CMK for the pilot. For now we can proceed with Redwood-managed keys if you provide an attestation.
[04:38] Priya: Noted. We'll include an encryption attestation doc.
[04:42] Jesse: Quick note on SOC2 — you asked for specific evidence earlier. Michael, can you remind the list again?
[04:49] Michael: Sure. We're looking for: SOC2 summary and last audit date, list of controls around access management, evidence of encryption at rest/in transit, incident response runbook example, and a sample of audit logs for typical user activity.
[05:02] Priya: We have a SOC2 summary in the security pack, plus a controls mapping table. The full report is under NDA but we can start with the summary and controls mapping.
[05:12] Jesse: We'll coordinate an NDA if you want the full report. For the POC checklist we'll send the summary and the controls mapping.
[05:20] Samir: Sounds good. A couple of integration questions — does the audit log include model variant info so we can correlate cost spikes to specific models?
[05:26] Priya: Yes, model_variant is included per request and we also emit a route tag. If you need token-level cost breakdowns, that's available as an additional export shape.
[05:38] Leah: Ok that will help. On authentication to the audit export API, do you support API keys scoped to read-only exports or do we need a service account?
[05:46] Priya: We support scoped API keys and short-lived service tokens. For automated SIEM ingestion we typically recommend a scoped API key that only has read:audit_logs permission.
[05:57] Michael: Good. Please include recommended key rotation cadence in the security doc.
[06:01] Jesse: Will do.
[06:03] [06:03] Priya: For the sample export we'll include field descriptions and an example of how to parse nested JSON in the route metadata; sometimes route metadata is JSON encoded as a string and that trips parser scripts.
[06:16] Samir: Noted, that happened to us with another vendor.
[06:20] Leah: One more thing — for the pilot we want to ensure data residency for EU traffic. How does Redwood route regionally?
[06:28] Jesse: At the moment for hosted POC we can pin routes to regionally proxied endpoints in EU or US. We can set routing policy so EU traffic stays in EU region and logs are stored in EU. For Private it's obviously under your VPC.
[06:42] Michael: We'll want that for the EU subset of users. Can you add region routing to the POC config?
[06:48] Priya: Yes, we'll add a route with region_hint = EU and include the config snippet in the doc.
[06:56] Jesse: Great. Anything else on security/compliance?
[06:59] Michael: One outstanding procurement question — do you have a standard BAa or data processing addendum?
[07:06] Jesse: Yes, we have a DPA and BAA templates. We'll attach them; signatures are usually via DocuSign.
[07:12] Leah: Ok thanks. On timeline — we want SSO working and a sample audit export by end of month to start internal tests. Is that feasible?
[07:20] Priya: Feasible. Action items we covered: Priya to share audit sample, Jesse to share SSO quickstart and security pack, Leah to provision IdP.
[07:30] Samir: For the SOC2 walkthrough, can we schedule a 45-minute session with our audit team the week after next?
[07:36] Michael: Yes I'll confirm stakeholders and send availability.
[07:40] Jesse: Perfect. Quick notes about some minor transcription/typo stuff — the audit export field name might have historical alt names, Priya mentioned "evt_time" for older exports; we will normalize.
[07:53] Priya: Also small gotcha: if you enable full-text logging there are cost implications and additional retention controls. We'll flag that in the doc.
[08:03] Leah: Understood.
[08:05] Jesse: OK let's do a short recap and next steps.
[08:08] Jesse (recap): Priya will produce the audit log sample CSV and schema by 2025-06-27; Jesse will send SSO quickstart + SAML metadata + security pack by 2025-06-27; Leah will provision test IdP and invite Redwood by 2025-06-30; Michael will confirm SOC2 stakeholders and availability for a walkthrough by 2025-06-30.
[08:28] Michael: That's accurate.
[08:30] Leah: Yep, thanks.
[08:32] Samir: Thanks all.
[08:34] Jesse: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and update the POC tracker. Bye.

End of recording.
